refuted.claim: bitsavers jpr108-2024.bcd: 'Byte-histogram inspection of the .bcd shows a raw 6-bit BCD object stream (105 distinct byte values, 0x40 dominant), not readable Autocoder text.'
refuted.why: The histogram is real (1,392,339 bytes, 105 distinct values, 0x40 = 388,116 occurrences) but the inference is invalid: a raw byte histogram cannot tell you whether BCD text is present, because BCD text IS a 6-bit byte stream. Decoding the file through a standard IBM 1401/1410 BCD-to-character table yields large runs of plainly readable symbolic Autocoder source. I counted 8,838 lines matching the Autocoder library card format (4-digit sequence number + mnemonic), concentrated in the first ~500 KB, with mnemonics DCW, DC, BOOL, MEND, MATH, NOTE, ORG, LTORG and IOCS macro names (IOCSDUMP50, IOCSLOAD50, HOLDNOW IOCTL). The image also decodes to '1410 AUTOCODER LIBRARY LISTING', 'AUTOCODER VERSION       LIBRARY LISTING', and the FORTRAN diagnostic message tables.
refuted.correction: jpr108-2024.bcd contains a substantial body of readable symbolic Autocoder text - the PR-108 system tape's Autocoder macro/IOCS library, which is genuinely source. What it does NOT contain is the FORTRAN compiler's own source: the FORTRAN phases are present only as object code plus their message tables. The finder's headline conclusion (no 1410 FORTRAN compiler source survives) is unaffected, but the supporting evidence and the method behind it should be discarded.
refuted.source: http://bitsavers.org/bits/IBM/1410/1410-PR-108/jpr108-2024.bcd (local copy, 1,392,339 bytes, decoded with the standard IBM BCD 6-bit character table); directory listing confirmed at http://bitsavers.org/bits/IBM/1410/1410-PR-108/

refuted.claim: 'The Catalog of Programs C20-1602-8 ... adds the crucial direction of the only documented trade: options are available to trade 1, 2, or 3 magnetic tape units for the 1402 and 1403 unit record devices - i.e. you may give up card/print devices and use MORE tape, never fewer.' / 'The tape requirement is architectural, not incidental.'
refuted.why: The directional reading is correct for the TAPE Processor Operating System (PR-108) - I confirmed it in a primary source below. But the blanket statement 'never fewer' and 'architectural' is refuted for the DISK Processor Operating System (PR-134), the host of 1410-FO-945. J28-0243 p.11 gives the disk POS minimum as 40,000 positions, Processing Overlap and Priority, 2 magnetic tape units and 50 cylinders of 1301, then footnotes exactly the opposite trade: 'Users who do not have tape units can substitute an IBM 1402 Card-Read Punch, Model 2, and a 1403 Printer, Model 2, for these two tape units.' C20-1602-8 repeats this verbatim for the disk COBOL processor 1410-CB-944, and the catalog's disk Autocoder (1410-AU-942) and disk RPG (1410-RG-943) minimum configurations list NO magnetic tape units at all - 40K, overlap and priority, 50 cylinders of 1301, one 1402, one 1403.
refuted.correction: The correct generalization is: every 1410 language processor requires bulk external system residence, but that residence may be either four-plus magnetic tape units (tape POS / PR-108) OR a 1301 disk module (disk POS / PR-134), and IBM explicitly documents a ZERO-TAPE disk configuration. The project-scope conclusion is unchanged - the announced CPU + 1402 + 1403 + 1415 has neither tape nor 1301 - but the reason is 'no bulk system-residence device', not 'tape is architecturally required'.
refuted.source: IBM J28-0243, 'IBM 1410 Operating System Using Magnetic Tape and 1301 Disk Storage' (1962), pp. 9-11 - http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/J28-0243_1410_Operating_System_Using_Magnetic_Tape_and_1301_Disk_Storage_1962.pdf ; IBM C20-1602-8 pages A-1410 005-006 - http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C20-1602-8_1410_pgmCatJun68.pdf

refuted.claim: Table row: '1410-FO-138 | 1410 FORTRAN Subroutine Library | ordered with FO-913 / FO-945 | ... | tape-resident | ... | contains the relocation loader + execution subroutines'.
refuted.why: The catalog's own FO-138 entry says the opposite about its distribution form. Verbatim: 'THE DISTRIBUTION OF THE FORTRAN SUBROUTINE LIBRARY IS IN CARDS IN ABSOLUTE FORMAT. THE AUTOCODER MIXED OUTPUT TAPE FOR 1410-FO-138 CONTAINING THE LIBRARY SUBROUTINE AND THE RELOCATABLE LOADER /TOTAL OF 51 FILES/ IS NO LONGER TO BE INCLUDED IN ANSWER TO REQUESTS FOR THE 1410 FORTRAN SUBROUTINE LIBRARY. HOWEVER, THE TAPE IS AVAILABLE AS AN OPTIONAL PROGRAM ITEM FOR THOSE WHO REQUEST SYMBOLIC LISTINGS AND PROGRAM DECKS.' FO-138 is also separately orderable by its own file number, not merely bundled.
refuted.correction: As of C20-1602-8 (Jun 1968) the FORTRAN Subroutine Library including the relocatable loader is distributed as a CARD deck in absolute format; the Autocoder mixed-output TAPE (51 files, library + relocatable loader, with symbolic listings) is an optional item. Note this cuts directly against the finder's own open question 1: card distribution of the loader and library weakens the assumption that the FO-913 execution path must be tape-resident. It does not settle it - the loader may still require a library tape at load time; C20-1602-8 notes 'APPENDIX C CONTAINS INSTRUCTIONS FOR CONSTRUCTING AND MAINTAINING A FORTRAN LIBRARY TAPE.'
refuted.source: IBM C20-1602-8, 'Catalog of Programs for IBM 1410', Jun 1968, 1410-FO-138 entry, IBM Programs section page A-1410 003/004 - http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C20-1602-8_1410_pgmCatJun68.pdf

refuted.claim: '-3.14159 [is stored] as the same ten digits with the sign carried as a zone over the low-order position' / table row 'Sign of the number | zone (over-punch) on the low-order position'.
refuted.why: I rendered C28-0328-3 page 8 at 1000 dpi and read the over-marks directly. The ten digits (3141590001) are correct - the finder's digits were right and the OCR that suggested '...51' was garbage. But there are FOUR over-marks, not one, and the number's sign is not on the low-order position of the word. For +3.14159: an inverted circumflex over position 1 (the '3'), a plus over position 8 (the low-order FRACTION digit), an inverted circumflex over position 9 (the high-order EXPONENT digit), and a plus over position 10. For -3.14159 the only change is that position 8's mark becomes a minus bar; positions 9 and 10 are unchanged. A22-0526-3 states the manual convention: 'each character that has an associated word mark has the inverted circumflex (v) above it.'
refuted.correction: Layout of an OS FORTRAN real value in f+2 core positions: word mark on position 1 (high-order fraction digit); fraction in positions 1..f with an understood decimal point before position 1; the MANTISSA's algebraic sign as a zone over position f (the low-order fraction digit); a SECOND word mark on position f+1 (high-order exponent digit), so the 2-digit exponent is its own word; and the EXPONENT's sign as a zone over position f+2. The low-order position of the whole word therefore carries the exponent's sign, not the number's. For the integer case, +314 with k=5 is 00314 with a word mark over the leading 0 and the sign zone over the units digit - the finder had the sign right there but missed the word mark.
refuted.source: IBM C28-0328-3, 'IBM 1410/7010 Operating System: FORTRAN' (Dec 1965), p. 8, rendered at 1000 dpi from http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C28-0328-3_1410_Fortran.pdf ; word-mark notation from IBM A22-0526-3, 'IBM 1410 Principles of Operation', 'Word Marks' - http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf

upgraded.claim: The trade footnote 'options are available to trade 1, 2, or 3 magnetic tape units for the 1402 and 1403 unit record devices' means additional tape units substitute FOR the unit-record devices (more tape, fewer card/print units) - not that tapes may be surrendered. Four tape units is a hard floor for the PR-108 tape system.
upgraded.source: IBM J28-0243 (1962) p.9 states the tape POS minimum as 20,000 positions, 4 tape units, one 1402 Model 2 and one 1403 Model 2, then 'NOTE 1: One tape unit each may be substituted for the card reader, the card punch, and the printer' - exactly the '1, 2, or 3' of the catalog footnote - and Figure 3 adds 'The minimum tape requirement for a tape-oriented system is 6 tape units.' Corroborated in C20-1602-8 by the FO-950 entry ('ONE 1402 CARD READ PUNCH MODEL 2 /OR A TAPE UNIT/ AND, ONE 1403 MODEL 2 /OR A TAPE UNIT/') and by the disk AU-942/RG-943 entries, whose base configuration contains zero tape units yet carries the same 'trade 1 or 2 or 3 magnetic tape units for the 1402 and 1403' footnote. http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/J28-0243_1410_Operating_System_Using_Magnetic_Tape_and_1301_Disk_Storage_1962.pdf

upgraded.claim: The real-constant digit string in C28-0328-3 is 3141590001 (fraction 31415900, exponent 01) for f=8 - i.e. a plain signed 2-digit power of ten, NOT an excess-50 or biased exponent.
upgraded.source: Read directly off the page at 1000 dpi; the archive OCR of that line ('5l4159005i' / '3141590651') is corrupt and had suggested an exponent of 51. The plain-signed reading is consistent with the manual's stated magnitude range of 10^-100 to (1-10^-f) x 10^99 (0.1 x 10^-99 = 10^-100), which excess-50 would not produce. IBM C28-0328-3 pp.7-8 - http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C28-0328-3_1410_Fortran.pdf

upgraded.claim: 1410 sign-zone convention that the FORTRAN storage format relies on: minus is always a B bit; plus may be B and A bits, no zone bits, or (less commonly) an A bit; machine-developed signs are BA for plus and B for minus.
upgraded.source: IBM A22-0526-3, 'IBM 1410 Principles of Operation', 'Sign Change or Development' and Figure 11 - http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf

additions.claim: The 1410 Autocoder itself (1410-AU-906) requires four magnetic tape units. C20-1602-8: 'MACHINE CONFIGURATION 1. 20K STORAGE. 2. FOUR IBM MAGNETIC TAPE UNITS. 3. AN IBM 1402. 4. AN IBM 1403.' with the same trade footnote. The catalog also notes of PR-108 that 'THE 1410 AUTOCODER HAS THE LARGEST MINIMUM REQUIREMENT' of the programs on the system tape, and the System Supervisor SV-907 needs 20K plus two tape units plus a 1402. So it is not only FORTRAN that cannot run on a card-only 1410 - no PR-108 processor can, the historical assembler included. This is the strongest single argument for the project's TypeScript Autocoder.
additions.source: IBM C20-1602-8, Jun 1968, IBM Programs page A-1410 004 (1410-AU-906 and 1410-SV-907 abstracts) - http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C20-1602-8_1410_pgmCatJun68.pdf

additions.claim: J28-0243, 'IBM 1410 Operating System Using Magnetic Tape and 1301 Disk Storage' (1962), is the pre-OS Processor Operating System bulletin the finder was missing, it IS on bitsavers, and unlike almost every other 1410 manual there it HAS a real text layer (pdftotext yields 37 KB). It gives, in one place: tape POS minimum = 20,000 positions + 4 tape units (729 II/IV/V or 7330, intermixable) + 1402 Model 2 + 1403 Model 2, with one tape substitutable for each of card reader, card punch and printer, and punch+print combinable on one tape preceded by a self-loading 1401 program; 'the minimum tape requirement for a tape-oriented system is six tape units'; disk POS minimum = 40,000 positions + Processing Overlap and Priority + 2 tape units + 50 cylinders of 1301 (15 consecutive cylinders for the system, 35 for working storage across up to three modules), with the 1402+1403-for-two-tapes substitution. It also states 'the final phase of the FORTRAN, COBOL and RPG processors consists of program assembly and/or macro-expansion handled by the Autocoder Processor' and that 'intermediate processing takes place on three work tapes'.

Both pre-OS FORTRAN compilers are demonstrably present on the surviving bitsavers PR-108 image, with version stamps recoverable from it: the 20K compiler emits '* COMPILED BY FORTRAN II, #1410-FO-913, VERSION 05 LEVEL00' and the 40K compiler emits 'COMPILED BY FORTRAN40K , 1410-FO-950  VERSION 01 LEVEL 08'. The image also carries the 40K processor's system-tape catalog entry ('FORTRAN40K') and the FORTRAN diagnostic message table ('***BAD NAME IN FORTRAN SOURCE STATEMENT', 'INVALID FORTRAN CHARACTER', 'END FORTRAN COMPILATION', 'LAST OBJECT LOCATIONS PROGRAM 00000 COMMON 00000').
additions.source: http://bitsavers.org/bits/IBM/1410/1410-PR-108/jpr108-2024.bcd, decoded with the standard IBM BCD table

additions.claim: The two surviving PR-108 tape images are NOT the same artifact: Paul Pierce's 'Autocoder System Tape w/OSP' data file is 4,616,734 bytes, while bitsavers jpr108-2024.bcd is 1,392,339 bytes. Any claim about 'the' PR-108 image should say which. (Pierce's tape labels read 'Autocoder System Tape w/OSP', created 5-24-68, recreated 4-9-70, permanent reel 188; Pierce's note corrects the label to POS and warns 'don't let my item identification code fool you, this is for the 1410 not the 1401'.)

Sky-visions publishes PR-108 FORTRAN sample jobs the finder did not list: alongside 'Fixed to run 20k Fortran', 'Job to enable 40k Fortran' and 'Job to enable 20k Fortran', the PR108 download block also offers 'Fortran Hello world' and 'Fortran Prime Numbers' jobs, plus a Simulator init file, an Autocoder test job and a sample COBOL program. If the project ever wants a reproduction target, those are the concrete artifacts.

Pre-OS integer semantics differ from the OS version in ways that matter if the demo borrows the format: J24-1468-1 says a fixed-point variable exceeding k digits 'is treated modulo 10^k' (the OS manual phrases the same behavior as 'the high-order digits are lost'); a fixed-point constant appearing in an expression 'is limited to 45 digits'; and when a fixed-point constant is used as a subscript value 'only five digits will be used'. Floating-point precision f defaults to 8 with a documented example of f=18 giving 'a 20-digit floating-point number, 18 for the mantissa and 2 for the characteristic'.
additions.source: IBM J24-1468-1, 'IBM 1410 FORTRAN', p.6 ('Arithmetic Precision', Figures 3-6) - http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/J24-1468-1_1410fortran.pdf

additions.claim: The catalog's FO-950 execution requirement is slightly softer than quoted: the second tape 'IS USED AS A WORK FILE BY THE LOADER AT LOAD TIME AND IS THEN AVAILABLE TO THE OBJECT PROGRAM' - the finder's quote stopped before the last clause. The loader/library tape is still permanently occupied.
additions.source: IBM C20-1602-8, Jun 1968, IBM Programs page A-1410 004 (1410-FO-950 abstract) - http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C20-1602-8_1410_pgmCatJun68.pdf

additions.claim: For the disk-oriented 1410/7010 OS the two required tape units are needed only for system generation: C28-0318-3 adds 'because the two magnetic tape units listed above are required only for generation of the system, they may serve other system functions during the day's processing... One of the tape units could be used in place of the card reader, and the other in place of the printer.' This does not lower the 60,000-position / one-1301-module floor.
additions.source: IBM C28-0318-3, 'IBM 1410/7010 Operating System: Basic Concepts' (Nov 1965), p.6 - http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C28-0318-3_1410_basicConcep.pdf

additions.claim: bitsavers /pdf/ibm/1410/ also holds C28-0328-1 (the earlier edition of the OS FORTRAN manual) and N27-1269, a TNL update to C28-0328-3. Neither was examined by the finder or by me; a TNL is exactly the kind of document that would revise the k and f ranges. Treat '3<=f<=18, 3<=k<=20' as correct for C28-0328-3 as printed, not necessarily as of the last TNL.
additions.source: http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/ (directory listing, retrieved 2026-08-29); N27-1269 referenced as 'Fortran Update' at http://www.sky-visions.com/ibm/ibm7010_soft.shtml

notes:
Method: nearly everything was checkable against primary text already extracted to the scratchpad (archive OCR of J24-1468-1, C28-0328-3, C20-1602-8, C28-0318-3, A22-0526-3), plus fresh fetches of J28-0243 and C28-0287-1, the bitsavers and Pierce directory listings, sky-visions, and the GitHub org API. Where OCR was garbled on a load-bearing detail I rendered the page from the PDF at 400-1000 dpi and read it, rather than trusting the text layer.

What held up: the four-processor taxonomy (FO-913, FO-950, FO-945, FO-970); J24-1468-1 p.5 machine requirements verbatim; the PR-108 program list; the FO-913 and FO-950 catalog configurations and the timing table; the FO-945/C26-0287 deferral and the FO-138 ordering requirement; the C28-0318-3 OS floors; the C28-0328-3 deferral to C28-0352; the optional-material listing tapes for FO-913, FO-950 and FO-945; the Pierce five-tape inventory; the bitsavers /pdf and /bits directory contents; the sky-visions summary; and the IBM-1401 GitHub org being 1401-only (all ten repos are 1401 tooling - autocoder, disasm, tpdump, dump, g-dump, 3to5, 5to3, autocoder_1401, Fortran-v3m0, Fortran-v3m4). I found no 1401-for-1410 substitution anywhere in the finder's facts; the one place the risk was real (the GitHub repos) the finder had already flagged it. Note in passing that the 1401 does appear legitimately inside 1410 documentation - PR-108 listing tapes carry 'THE SELF LOADING 1401 PROGRAM WHICH PRINTS AND PUNCHES THE CONTENTS OF THE TAPE', and combined punch/print output tapes are meant for offline 1401 processing - so a 1401 mention in a 1410 context is not automatically an error.

What I could not settle: open question 1 (can an FO-913 object deck run on a tapeless 20K 1410). C28-0287-1_1410_osWith1301.pdf on bitsavers has no OCR text layer, and J28-0243 - which does have one - never discusses object-deck loading or the relocatable loader. The new FO-138 card-distribution fact above is the only real movement on it, and it points toward 'maybe', not 'yes'. Open question 4 (a listing tape surviving outside the searched archives) remains untestable from here; a targeted web search for recovered 1410 FORTRAN compiler source returned only 1401 material.

One caution on my own strongest finding: the 8,838 Autocoder-format lines in jpr108-2024.bcd are the system's macro/IOCS library, which I sampled but did not exhaustively classify. I am confident they are not FORTRAN compiler source (the FORTRAN regions of the image decode to object code and message tables), but if the project cares, that image is worth a proper pass with a correct 1410 BCD table and the tape's own file structure - it is 1.4 MB and clearly holds more recoverable symbolic material than anyone has claimed.
